newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil new CVRD board of directors takes office.
newsitem.headline: Brazil new CVRD board of directors takes office.

text.p: A CVRD shareholder assembly has voted in the company's new board of directors, appointing the chairman of steelmaker CSN, Benjamin Steinbruch, as the new company chairman, a CVRD spokesman said.
CSN led the Valepar consortium which placed the winning bid of $3.15 billion for 41.73 percent of CVRD voting stock at the May 6 privatization auction on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange.

At the shareholder assembly, Steinbruch said CVRD would be interested in participating in upcoming privatizations in the electricity and natural gas sectors to secure its energy supply, a CSN spokesman said.

The new board of directors has nine members of which two represent CSN, four are representatives of Valepar's group of pension funds, one represents Valepar member Opportunity Asset Management and the other two seats went to representatives of CVRD's employees, the CVRD spokesman said.

Jair Bilachi, the president of Brazil's largest pension fund, Previ, was appointed vice-chairman of CVRD, CSN Director Maria Silvia Bastos Marques is the second CSN representative and former Central Bank president Persio Arida speaks for Opportunity.

CVRD's management team, including company President Francisco Schettino, will remain unchanged for now as Valepar plans to spend the next six months studying CVRD in depth before carrying out any changes, the CVRD spokesman said.

The shareholder assembly also approved the allocation of 85 million reais ($80.2 million) to a 200 million reais ($188.7 million) fund which will finance infrastructure and social works in 237 municipalities in nine states where CVRD operates, the CVRD spokesman said.

Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES) will provide the remaining 115 million reais ($108.5 million) to the fund, which replaces CVRD's obligation prior to privatization to spend eight percent of its annual net profit on social projects.
